assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED recast cavity QED in an on-chip setting: a superconducting qubit strongly coupled to a microwave resonator gives dispersive readout, qubit-qubit coupling through a bus, and the architecture now used in most superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear, original, widely reproduced concept with direct experimental and technological consequences, and it is distinct from the macroscopic quantum tunnelling work recognised in 2025.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues) are the decisive steps. Blais as theorist, Wallraff as first experimental demonstrator and Schoelkopf as leader of the Yale programme form a coherent trio. Girvin and Huang are not in the supplied credit, so the theory share is only partly represented, and the Yale group credit is shared among many.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of independent confirmation across many laboratories, plus the standard transmon and readout toolbox built on it. Recognition is timely, though the 2025 prize in the same broad area may argue for some pause.
uncertainties: I work in this field and know several of these people by reputation, so I may overvalue it relative to other fields.
Whether the committee wants a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025 is unclear.
Allocation between theory (Blais, Girvin) and experiment is open and the supplied names omit some contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned a foundational property of quantum states into a cryptographic protocol whose security rests on physical law, and it launched quantum communication as a field. BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol are clear and original, and the lasting impact on both foundations and experiment is considerable.
assessment.attribution: BB84 is by Bennett and Brassard, with an important antecedent in Wiesner's unpublished conjugate-coding idea (Wiesner is not in the supplied credit). Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent route linked to Bell tests. Three names give a plausible configuration, but the Wiesner priority issue is a genuine sensitivity.
assessment.maturity: Experimental QKD has been demonstrated over fibre and satellite links, with commercial systems. Practical security against device imperfections is still being developed, but the concept is mature and well confirmed.
uncertainties: Priority of Wiesner's earlier idea and his absence from the credit.
Whether Ekert should share with Bennett and Brassard or whether the prize should go to BB84 alone.
Practical security loopholes may lead some members to see applications as less decisive than the physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combined the magic-wavelength idea with many atoms interrogated at once, giving fractional uncertainty at or below 1e-18. It has changed precision measurement, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy, and is a clear, concrete instrument-and-concept achievement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and realised the first strontium clocks; Ye's group drove the record stability and accuracy and the spectroscopy of many-body effects. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though Hall and Hänsch (2005) and the broader clock community, including ion-clock work by others, complicate perceived novelty.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have confirmed the performance, and redefinition of the second is under discussion. Maturity is strong, with the redefinition still to come.
uncertainties: The overlap with earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock recognition may lead to a debate about novelty.
Other contributors to lattice clocks, such as theorists on magic wavelengths, are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator opened a field of topological band theory, with a clear theoretical prediction followed by direct experimental confirmation. The concept is original and has reshaped condensed-matter physics and links to topological quantum computation.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 invariant; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal (BHZ are not in this entry). The theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, but the omission of Bernevig, Zhang and Hughes and of the 3D insulator work of Moore, Balents, Fu, Hasan makes the allocation contested.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in 2D and 3D materials, with a large body of follow-up experiments. The field is mature, though practical use is modest.
uncertainties: Attribution is contested: BHZ and the 3D topological insulator discoverers are outside the supplied credit.
The 2016 prize on topological phases may lead some to feel the area is already recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was the central goal of the LHC. Its significance is beyond doubt, and the physics verification of the mechanism proposed in the 1960s is one of the most important results of the period.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists. Experimental credit is spread over thousands of collaborators, with a limit of three laureates. Founders and leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are a defensible choice, but Gianotti as spokesperson at the time of announcement is also a strong claim. The configuration is thus difficult and only partly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and thoroughly confirmed through coupling measurements. Recognition has been awaited for years and is a long-standing gap.
uncertainties: The three-laureate limit against a large collaboration makes any allocation arguable.
Choice between founding spokespersons and those at announcement is unresolved by the supplied credit.
This is far from my own expertise, so I rely on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a very active and original field with a tunable platform for correlation physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the continuum-model prediction (2011) and Jarillo-Herrero's group the 2018 experiments, with Cao, Fatemi et al. as the first authors. The trio is logical, but other groups (Dean, Young, Yacoby, Kim, and others) reported important follow-up and fractional Chern insulator results.
assessment.maturity: Strong replication since 2018, but the field is still evolving, with unresolved mechanisms for superconductivity. Probably slightly early compared with the older candidates.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains debated.
Credit to other experimental groups and to Cao and Fatemi as the leading students is not captured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulation of many-body states including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and, more recently, single-site resolved microscopy. It is original and links condensed matter and quantum information, which I find attractive.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation, Greiner and Bloch carried out the 2002 Mott transition experiment and developed quantum-gas microscopy, and Esslinger contributed fermionic Hubbard physics. Jaksch is not in the supplied credit, and four names exceed the limit, so my selection leaves out Esslinger.
assessment.maturity: The experiments are well confirmed, but the claim for solving open problems in strongly correlated matter is still partial. Recognition is plausible but not pressing given the 2001 and 2012 prizes in adjacent areas.
uncertainties: Credit among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is hard to separate, and Jaksch is absent.
Some argue that the simulators have not yet produced a decisive new result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic plane neutrino map, opened neutrino astronomy and gave a direct probe of cosmic-ray accelerators. It is a clear and important discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen has led the concept and the collaboration, with Karle and Spiering as key figures in construction and analysis. In such a large collaboration, decisive individual roles are hard to establish and the supplied credit cannot settle it. Other pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES) are not in the credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by repeated analyses, and the 2023 Galactic-plane result reinforces it. The source identification remains partial, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early.
uncertainties: The sources of most of the flux are still unidentified.
Collaboration-scale credit and prior neutrino-telescope pioneers complicate the choice of three names.
This is outside my own research area.
